correctness.rationale: C=S−E in every induced forest, yielding exact mean/variance formulas. Every cross-tree third raw-moment difference reduces to −E[E³], and counting the four three-edge configurations gives −6 delta(P4) p^4(1−p)^2. Equal mean/variance converts this to third-cumulant difference. Factors p^4,q^2,z,(z−1)^3 follow from subset/deletion boundary cases and equal low factorial moments, with coprimality over the integer polynomial ring. At n6 exactly the two indicated degree-matched trees exist and 64-subset exhaustive counts yield the full PGF factor. Python Prüfer enumeration checks 1/1/2/3/6 nonisomorphic classes and the finite moment identities. The proof, not the enumeration, covers all n and p.

value.rationale: Habitat fragmentation counts are natural ecological network observables. Equal degree distributions can conceal the whole first two count moments, so ecological models based only on degree/wedge summaries cannot detect this shape dependence. The exact P4-based third cumulant detects it for all 0<p<1, and the unique six-patch threshold proves it is already relevant in the smallest structurally ambiguous habitat trees. This is a motivated universality-and-sharp-boundary result, not a trivial Q polynomial recomputation. Homogeneous independent survival and unconditioned fragment counts delimit the value.
